entities.name: PMID:25083606
observations: In 36 IBS patients challenged with diluted food antigens during duodenal CLE, 22/36 developed increased intraepithelial lymphocytes, epithelial leaks/gaps, and widened intervillous spaces within 5 minutes; no reaction occurred in 14 CLE-negative IBS patients or 10 non-IBS controls.

entities.name: PMID:31100380
observations: In a prospective IBS food-challenge study, 76/108 completers were CLE-positive; findings included increased duodenal intraepithelial lymphocytes, increased claudin-2, reduced occludin, and increased eosinophil degranulation/eosinophilic cationic protein.

entities.name: PMID:34544843
observations: In a double-blind multicentre study of non-coeliac Rome III IBS patients exposed to wheat, soy, yeast, and milk during CLE, diagnostic sensitivity and specificity for wheat sensitivity were modest, so routine widespread diagnostic use was not supported.

entities.name: IBS food CLE response
observations: Direct duodenal food challenge during CLE can produce rapid mucosal changes in a subset of IBS patients, including epithelial leakage, increased intraepithelial lymphocytes, widened intervillous spaces, and altered barrier markers.

entities.name: CLE diagnostic limitation
observations: CLE demonstrates biological food-associated responses in IBS but has insufficient and inconsistent diagnostic accuracy for routine widespread identification of wheat sensitivity.
